subject: Recap + proposed eval sprint for Zephyr Health (next steps)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramesh <asha@zephyrhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + proposed eval sprint for Zephyr Health (next steps)

Hi Asha — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single, actionable plan: 

1) Key takeaways from our call
- Primary use case: automated clinical summarization + triage for care coordinators (sensitive PHI, strict retention rules).
- Target latency: sub-350ms token generation on 512-token median workload.
- Primary quality concern: hallucinations in medication and diagnosis extraction; recall > 95% on gold prompts.

2) Recommended 4-week eval sprint (high level)
- Week 0 (prep): exchange prompt bundle + sample dataset (we'll mask PHI).
- Week 1: baseline run vs. your proprietary model (1k sample prompts).
- Week 2: open-model trials (3 variants, quant profiles) + metric analysis.
- Week 3: focused error analysis, rerun top prompts, finalize acceptance readout.

3) Models we recommend trialing (initial set)
- r-infer-prop-7B (our Redwood-verified baseline; reference latency profile included)
- OpenLlama-3-13B (q4_8 or q4_K_M weights; good tradeoff for hallucination control)
- CodeFormer-7B-sft (strong on instructions, test if it reduces hallucination on extraction tasks)

4) Acceptance signals we expect to discuss (draft; can be tightened)
- Factual extraction recall >= 95% on labeled set
- Entity hallucination rate < 1.5%
- Mean latency per token within 20% of baseline SLA target

Attachments I uploaded for the sprint: MAP_Zephyr_Health_v1.docx (mutual action plan), prompt_set_zephyr_v2.json (sample prompts), benchmark_q1_sample.csv (sample metrics).

Please confirm: (A) the priority scenarios you want included in the 1k seed, (B) whether procurement should be looped in now (I cc'd procurement alias per your note), and (C) availability for a 30-min kickoff on Apr 4 or Apr 5.

Thanks — I can move Epic/HubSpot to "Evaluate" stage once we lock the kickoff.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Asha Ramesh <asha@zephyrhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + proposed eval sprint for Zephyr Health (next steps)

Thanks Connor — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick items from our side:

- We definitely want the medication & diagnosis extraction scenarios prioritized for the 1k seed.
- Parity thresholds: our clinical QA team will push back if hallucination > 1%, but we can be pragmatic and accept <=1.5% for the moment if the tradeoff is substantial latency reduction.
- Procurement (procurement@zephyrhealth.com) is looped in; they want a short one-pager on data handling and SLA before signing the MAP.

Can you confirm that any data we share for the 1k seed will be handled under a limited-use testing agreement and destroyed after the sprint? Also curious if Redwood can run the baseline compare against our proprietary model without us uploading raw data (we prefer on-prem evaluation if possible).

Asha Ramesh
Director, Clinical AI | Zephyr Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Asha Ramesh <asha@zephyrhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed eval sprint for Zephyr Health (next steps) — acceptance metrics & test plan

Hi Asha — following up with concrete metrics and the measurement plan so procurement and clinical QA can review. I pushed the measurement harness and a small example result to the Drive link in the MAP.

Measurement plan (summary)
- Data handling: we'll use masked, synthetic-preserving samples for the exploratory runs. Any raw PHI can be processed in your VPC deployment or with an encrypted transfer; we will delete test artifacts after the sprint and provide a deletion certificate.
- Metrics we will compute per prompt set: recall (entity-level), precision, exact-match rate (for extracted fields), hallucination-rate (external facts not in prompt), and a qualitative error taxonomy.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposal)
  * Entity recall >= 95% (primary)
  * Hallucination rate <= 1.5% (ideally <=1%)
  * Regression tolerance vs your proprietary baseline: no more than 3% relative drop on clinical recall for core extraction scenarios
  * Latency: median p50 generation latency within 25% of your SLA target for median prompt length

Models to include in the first trial batch (rationales)
- r-infer-prop-7B: Redwood baseline to provide a calibrated comparison for latency and hallucination tradeoffs.
- OpenLlama-3-13B (q4_K_M): strong instruction-following, good factuality with the right prompt templates.
- Anthropic-legacy-7B-sft (if you can share a redacted sample): added as a different family to test hallucination failure modes.

Prompt bundles
- prompt_set_zephyr_v2.json (attached) — canonical extraction prompts + negative examples
- prompt_set_clinical_edgecases.json (we will push once we collect your flagged cases)

Benchmarks and links
- HubSpot run & artifacts: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/ZPH-2027-042
- Eval harness (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-eval-link-zw-health

Procurement notes: I'll prepare a short one-pager (data handling + deletion certificate) and loop legal for the limited-use testing agreement. Connor — can you add procurement's timeline into the MAP?

— Soojin
Soojinn Lee
Head of Model Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Connor — procurement here. A few items to close before we approve the MAP and kickoff:

1) SLA/uptime: do you have a short SLA stub for the eval environment (availability targets during the sprint)?
2) Data retention: confirm the deletion certificate process and whether the deletion certificate will be signed by Redwood legal.
3) Cost: approximate spend cap we should expect for the 4-week sprint (tokens + instance hours).
4) Contract path: are you proposing a MAP + SOW + MSA (we prefer to see a single SOW w/ MAP as appendix)?

Please provide answers in-line; we need a short one-pager to attach to our internal approval packet.

Procurement
Zephyr Health

Thanks all — summary answers below and proposed next steps so procurement has the one-pager they asked for. I've attached the MAP doc which includes the SOW outline.

Procurement Q&A (short)
1) SLA/uptime for eval environment: 99% availability during business hours in the region selected for the sprint (US), with monitoring dashboards provided via Redwood Console. This is an evaluation SLA; production SLAs are available under Dedicated/Private contracts.
2) Data retention & deletion certificate: Redwood will provide a deletion certificate within 48 hours of confirmed deletion. For PHI-only runs we recommend an on-prem or VPC-forwarded evaluation; we can sign a Limited Use Testing Agreement prior to any transfer.
3) Cost: estimated cap for the 4-week sprint: $8k–$12k depending on runtime profile selected (we'll confirm exact estimate after we lock model/quant choices).
4) Contract path: MAP + SOW (one SOW with MAP as Appendix) — we'll surface a draft MSA if procurement requires it but the MAP + SOW should be sufficient for the sprint approval.

Next steps / asks
- Procurement: if the one-pager below looks good I can mark the HubSpot deal stage to "MAP signed" and send a DocuSign link for the MAP (link: https://docusign.com/sign/ZPH-MAP-2027).
- Asha / Clinical QA: confirm the 1k seed scenarios (meds + diagnosis extraction) today if possible; otherwise we push kickoff to Apr 5.
- Internal: Soojin — can you run the baseline compare plan after Asha provides the masked seed? Marissa — I'll add the acceptance thresholds into the HubSpot playbook.

Proposed kickoff: Apr 4 at 10:00 AM PT (30 min). If Apr 4 doesn't work, Apr 5 in the morning is fine.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
